project.projectDesc: Scores Bitcoin-related tweet sentiment and compares daily sentiment trends with Bitcoin price data.

caseStudy.summary: This academic project scores Bitcoin-related social-media sentiment and compares daily sentiment trends with Bitcoin price data. The notebook uses AFINN sentiment scoring and time-based aggregation to explore whether sentiment and price move together.
caseStudy.challenge: Social posts are noisy and informal, and sentiment changes over time while market prices fluctuate continuously. The analysis needed to convert text into consistent sentiment labels and align the resulting series with price observations.
caseStudy.architecture: The notebook loads sentiment and Bitcoin price CSV files, maps AFINN scores to positive, neutral, and negative labels, aggregates sentiment by day, and compares the resulting series with price data.
caseStudy.diagram:
flowchart LR
  Tweets[Bitcoin-related posts] --> Scoring[AFINN sentiment scoring]
  Scoring --> Daily[Daily sentiment aggregation]
  Prices[Bitcoin price data] --> Align[Date alignment]
  Daily --> Align
  Align --> Analysis[Trend comparison]
  Analysis --> Findings[Exploratory observations]
contributions: Implemented a Python notebook for sentiment scoring and time-based analysis.
Mapped AFINN scores into positive, neutral, and negative sentiment labels.
Aggregated sentiment by day and compared it with Bitcoin price trends.
Used pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and Seaborn for data preparation and analysis.
tradeoffs: A lexicon-based method is transparent and lightweight but can miss sarcasm, context, and crypto-specific meaning.
Daily aggregation makes trends easier to compare but hides intraday changes.
The notebook describes exploratory association, not evidence that sentiment causes price movement.

scale: The supplied resume describes analysis of approximately 2.5 million Bitcoin-related tweets.
